edit.find: The WRAM map describes hpToHeal as a heal request that the HUD plays out as the HP recovery animation; no reader of $0B22 was found in extracted/, so that is documentation only (see the questions file).
edit.with: hpToHeal ($0B22) is a heal request that UpdateHUD (UpdateHUD_Active in system_core) plays out: on every 8th frame, unless the game-over bit of playerStateByte is set, a nonzero hpToHeal is decremented by one and playerHp is incremented by one with sound $0D; when playerHp equals playerMaxHp the request is cleared instead. The $0040 written here is therefore a request for up to 64 points of HP, capped at playerMaxHp.

edit.find: loads operand slot +2 when the player is more than 15 px WEST of the actor, +6 when more than 15 px EAST and +4 when within 15 px (including 0).
edit.with: loads operand slot +2 when the player is 15 px or more WEST of the actor, +6 when 15 px or more EAST and +4 when |dx| is below 15 (including 0); the threshold test is CMP [$0A] / BCC, so |dx| = 15 already takes the outer slot.

edit.find: 6. The label pairs are named after the wrong axis:
edit.with: 6. The side word in the labels that contain Player<Side> (CollectGemAlignPlayerNorth, CollectGemNudgePlayerWestHalf, PushSolidMovePlayerSouth, PushForceballRestorePlayerEast ...) names the side of the object on which the player stands: North / South = the player is above / below (the same-column blocks, Y axis), West / East = the player is west / east (the same-row blocks, X axis). The object moves toward that side. In the North block and the West block of each handler the first BPL (d >= 0, to the South / East block) is followed by a second BPL to the label after the abs(); N is still set after the first BPL, so the second one is never taken and the abs() always runs for d < 0.

edit.find: Flags $0302: bit $0200 is part of the combat_collision skip masks (OQ-I030-2); $0100 and $0002 are undecoded.
edit.with: Flags $0302: bit $0200 is part of the combat_collision skip mask $76E0 (CombatCollision_InnerLoop); bit $0002 is the depth override SetPriorityMax, so SortActorsByDepth draws the particle in front of every other actor; bit $0100 is not traced.

edit.find: The older header named only the first two. docs/code/bank00/functions-camera-motion.md describes the routine as an LDX #8 / JSR random / DEX loop with offsets of +-$10 .. +-$30 pixels; the code is a COP LoopStart / LoopEnd script and the offsets are -16 .. +15 px.

No code that reads the actor bit was found (the Psycho Slider sets and clears the same bit), so the old claim that it "freezes movement" is unverified. docs/wram-memory-map.md lists "$0200 deathFlag, set by StopPlayerOnDeath" as a WRAM address; that entry confuses a bit mask with an address.
edit.with: The Psycho Slider sets and clears the same actor bit. The routine writes only playerSpeedEw, playerSpeedNs and the actor's $08 and $10; it never writes playerFlags.
